source_caption:
There’s Something About Mary became a comedy classic because it pushes embarrassment to absurd extremes while still keeping Mary genuinely lovable. Cameron Diaz plays her with such warmth and natural charm that the entire movie’s chaos makes sense — every man loses his mind around her, but the joke is always on their desperation, not on her.

There’s Something About Mary (1998), directed by Peter Farrelly & Bobby Farrelly, starring Cameron Diaz, Ben Stiller, Matt Dillon. A wildly outrageous romantic comedy about obsession, awkwardness, and impossible crushes, turning humiliation and slapstick into one of the defining comedies of the 1990s.

source_details.title: There's Something About Mary
source_details.synopsis: There's Something About Mary is a 1998 American romantic comedy film directed by the Farrelly brothers, who co-wrote the screenplay with Ed Decter and John J. Strauss. The film features Cameron Diaz as the title character, while Ben Stiller, Matt Dillon, Lee Evans, and Chris Elliott all play characters who are in love with Mary, and vying for her affection. There's Something About Mary was released theatrically on July 15, 1998, by 20th Century Fox. It received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its humor and Diaz's performance.
